Subject: Post-call recap + MAP draft next steps (MSA/DPA/SLA redlines)

Kate — thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum toward your Q2 integration target.

Call highlights:
- Scope confirmed: core inference (hosted) + dedicated capacity for PII workloads; SOC2 artifacts required for procurement.
- Primary dependencies: security questionnaire completion, procurement PO, and legal redline loop.

Proposed target close date: 2028-04-07 (we're flagging this in the MAP).

MAP milestone: MSA/DPA/SLA redlines — proposal
- Ownership (initial pass): DataWell does customer-side redlines for data handling / DPA specifics; Redwood will own SLA/ops sections and core MSA language for inference runtime.
- Turnaround expectation: 72 hours for first-pass review after receiving redlines; 72 hours for counter-redline. If a critical SLA clause is flagged, we escalate with a 24-hour response SLA for acknowledgement + plan.

Action items from Redwood:
- I will upload a DW-focused MAP draft (DW-MAP-v1.docx) and a tracked MSA with our suggested edits by EOD today (attachment).
- Ben will coordinate Legal and confirm who will produce the first tracked-change file if DataWell prefers to start the redline.

Please confirm: (a) whether DataWell prefers to submit MSA redlines into the Doc link I shared, or send a marked PDF; (b) whether 72h looks acceptable as a standard TAT.

Attaching meeting-notes-20280310.pdf for reference.

Thanks — looking forward to the quick turnaround so we can lock dates with Infra and CS.

Best,
Laura Bennett

Laura — thanks for the recap and the draft plan. Quick answers:
1) We typically prefer to produce the first set of MSA redlines (our legal team likes to start with data & liability language). Oliver (CC'd) will coordinate.
2) 72h for initial review is reasonable, though for very technical SLA items our procurement likes a 5-business-day review window. Can we mark SLA items as high/normal priority in the MAP so we can triage?

We'll look for the DW-MAP-v1 link and our legal team will aim to send the initial redline by next Tue 2028-03-14 EOD.

Thanks,
Kate Reynolds
Head of Platform Partnerships | DataWell
KReynolds@DataWell.com

On a process note, what's the preferred inbound: upload to the Doc you shared or send back a redlined PDF? We can do either but want to avoid duplicate work.

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Reynolds <kate@datawell.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@datawell.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + MAP draft next steps (MSA/DPA/SLA redlines)

Kate / Oliver — appreciate the quick feedback. To avoid dual-tracking, here's our suggested lightweight triage and routing approach (will put into the MAP doc as a matrix):

Redline routing matrix (suggested):
- MSA - Commercial & liability clauses -> DataWell initial redline OK; Redwood legal to respond (Owner: DataWell / Redwood TAT: 72h)
- DPA - Data processing terms, data location, subprocessors -> Owner: DataWell (initial) & Redwood (review); TAT: 72h
- SLA - latency/uptime/penalties -> Owner: Redwood for baseline language; DataWell to flag deviations. TAT: 72h for technical clarifications. Mark SLA items as High/Normal — high items get 48h triage acknowledgement and 72h formal response.
- Security artifacts (SOC2, pen test summary) -> Owner: Redwood to provide artifacts; TAT: immediate upload (we've attached SOC2-evidence.zip).

I uploaded DW-MAP-v1.docx and a living MSA with our baseline edits to the shared Doc here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcD-MAP-DW-v1. Please drop your redlines directly into the Doc (track changes) to speed reconciliation. If your counsel prefers a PDF, we can accept that but will convert into tracked changes for consistency.

Attachments: DW-MAP-v1.docx, Redlines_DW_MSA.pdf (baseline).

If this routing matrix looks good I will add explicit milestone dates into the MAP (first redline received -> Redwood counter -> final sign) and flag procurement PO as a blocking dependency.

Laura
